# Contributing to Two Hours One Life Data
Thank you for your interest in contributing to the data of Two Hours One
Life! These guidelines exist so that we have a mutual understanding of
expectations. This helps us to clear up confusion and be respectful of one
another's time.

## Licensing
By submitting a contribution to this repository or explicitly providing your
artwork to a contributor for addition to the game, you acknowledge and agree
that your work will be released into the public domain.

Please see `no_copyright.txt` for more information. Any questions or concerns
are welcome to be submitted to our Discord server.

## Tools
1. We work with Git on GitHub.
   1. You must have a basic understanding of Git and how to use it on GitHub.
      In particular you should be comfortable with opening a Pull Request,
      accepting feedback and adjusting your work until it satisfies a reviewer.
   2. [GitHub
      flow](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/using-github/github-flow) is
      a helpful reference process.
2. We communicate on our [Discord server](https://discord.gg/Jd9Es3f).
   1. Join our
      [#contributing-help](https://discord.com/channels/423293333864054833/919848284955234314)
      channel for any related questions.
3. We use a custom client to make changes to game data.
   1. This custom client is known as the Editor. Contributors must compile it
      themselves by following [this
      guide](https://github.com/risvh/miniOneLifeCompile).
   2. We require this because editing game data is a technical process.
      Compiling the Editor will help you understand how it works.
   3. Learn how to use the Editor [here](https://twohoursonelife.fandom.com/wiki/Editor_Guide).

## Guidelines
1. Before starting a change, consult the team in #contributing-help. You may
   then document your proposed change in a GitHub issue. This ensures
   that your change fits within the spirit of the game, providing
   the greatest chance that it will be accepted.
2. Report small bugs and suggestions on Discord instead of opening a pull
   request. Even small data changes require substantial testing and review.
3. Each pull request should contain one focused change, split into one or more
   logical commits. A narrow scope makes the pull request easier to review.
4. Make sure that you understand the distinction between content changes and
   code changes. See [this wiki article](https://twohoursonelife.fandom.com/wiki/Modding_Notes#Content_Changes_vs_Code_Changes).
5. First-time contributors are welcome to pick a task from the [list of starter
   tasks](https://github.com/orgs/twohoursonelife/projects/12/views/1). Please
   do not pick up these tasks if you are not a first-time contributor.
6. Experienced contributors may be granted access to #contributing-forum in our
   Discord server, where contributors privately collaborate on upcoming changes.
   The team grants access at its discretion, based on your knowledge of the game
   and history of playing and contributing.

- "The team" in this document refers to the core team of maintainers, found in
  our Discord server as "Core team".
